extracted.intended_audience: state, local, and other permitting programs that receive EPA financial assistance; EPA staff and managers with permit review responsibilities
extracted.subtask_description: Interim EPA FAQs describing how permitting programs should integrate environmental justice (EJ) and civil rights (especially Title VI) into permitting: screening, EJ/disparate-impact analyses, community engagement, tribal consultation, mitigation, and staff/recipient responsibilities. Intended to guide permit development, review, and remediation actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title VI disparate impact analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether a permit will have an adverse and disproportionate impact on the basis of race, color, or national origin (including LEP status), and evaluate whether there is a substantial and legitimate justification for any such disproportionate impact and whether a less discriminatory alternative exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The disparate impact analysis includes: (1) identifying disproportionate adverse impacts on protected classes; (2) assessing whether the recipient has a substantial, legitimate, nondiscriminatory justification for the impacts; and (3) evaluating whether a less discriminatory alternative is available. Consider cumulative impacts (see FAQ #12) and consult FAQs #11–13 for specific investigative and legal standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Screening using GIS and EJ mapping tools (e.g., EJScreen)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Geographic Information System (GIS) tools such as EPA’s EJScreen or state EJ mapping tools as a starting point to assess whether a permitting action raises environmental justice or civil rights concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EJScreen and state tools provide demographic and environmental data layers and highlight indices at the 80th, 90th, and 95th percentiles to benchmark potential disproportionate impacts relative to state, regional, and national averages. Use these tools to quickly assess and document community vulnerability and pollution burden and to support consistent approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and record responses to key screening questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Record answers to questions like: Is the affected population already experiencing disproportionate impacts? How likely are the permit's potential impacts to cause or contribute to disproportionate impacts?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early, documented screening responses support decisions on whether to proceed with more detailed EJ/disparate impact analyses and inform community engagement and mitigation planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review other readily available data in screening
rubrics_metrics.description: When screening suggests potential disproportionate impacts, review additional data beyond mapping indices to better characterize impacts and vulnerability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant data include: lists of other permitted facilities in the area (and whether they are major or minor sources), applicant compliance records, demographic data (race, national origin, age, LEP, income, education), environmental pollutant measurements (ambient concentrations, total loadings), presence of other significant emissions sources (ports, highways), facilities handling hazardous materials, and health data (mortality, asthma, infant mortality, low birth weight, unhoused populations, health care access).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider local knowledge and past community engagement in screening
rubrics_metrics.description: Use local knowledge and information from earlier engagement as core components of screening for EJ or civil rights concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish early, ongoing relationships with communities to gain trust and communication needed to solicit input from impacted residents, stakeholders, local agencies, and tribal governments. Local knowledge can reveal conditions not visible in datasets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider public complaints, media reports, and other community-sourced information
rubrics_metrics.description: Include complaints to federal/state/local authorities, media reports, and other local or national data sources when assessing potential EJ or civil rights concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complaints can pertain directly to the permitting action or reflect broader community conditions (e.g., high asthma rates or unemployment) that are relevant to assessing vulnerability and potential disproportionate impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct an appropriately scoped EJ analysis or disparate impact analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: If screening indicates concerns, undertake a more detailed EJ analysis and/or a Title VI disparate impact analysis sized to the issues identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The analysis should further evaluate who is affected, how and how much, comparisons to reference populations, potential mitigations, and inform enhanced community engagement. EJ analyses and disparate impact analyses may overlap but conduct separate Title VI analysis to satisfy civil rights obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise statutory and regulatory authority to prevent or mitigate adverse disproportionate impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Use available federal, state, and local statutory/regulatory authority and discretion in permitting to prevent or mitigate adverse and disproportionate impacts that could violate Title VI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where permit-based mitigation is available under environmental statutes/regulations, incorporate enforceable permit terms; where not sufficient, coordinate additional measures across agencies and programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate mitigation outside the permit when permit mitigation is insufficient
rubrics_metrics.description: When mitigation included in a permit is not sufficient to address adverse and disproportionate impacts that might violate Title VI, consider mitigation outside the permit by coordinating across agency programs, state agencies, community organizations, and NGOs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mitigations outside the permit may include public health programs, transportation plans, infrastructure projects, or other commitments implemented through interagency coordination or agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Health Impact Assessments (HIAs) and methodologies for EJ analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate methodologies such as health impact assessments and other promising practices when conducting EJ analyses to assess site-specific and cumulative impacts and possible mitigations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HIAs and similar methodologies can identify health, environmental, and quality-of-life impacts and support identifying mitigations and less discriminatory alternatives that may also inform Title VI evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include cumulative impacts in Title VI/disparate impact considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider cumulative impacts (the combined effect of multiple past, present, and reasonably foreseeable actions) when evaluating disparate impacts under Title VI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cumulative impacts can be relevant to whether a permit will cause or contribute to disproportionate harms; assess existing burdens from other sources and community vulnerabilities alongside the proposed action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permit term: enforceable continuous compliance monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Include enforceable requirements for continuous compliance monitoring equipment (e.g., opacity cameras) to ensure proper operation of controls and adherence to permitted limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuous monitoring can provide real-time assurance of compliance and serve as a tool for community transparency and enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permit term: enhancements to compliance assurance (monitoring, recordkeeping, reporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Strengthen compliance assurance through additional continuous or periodic monitoring, more detailed recordkeeping, and more frequent or transparent reporting requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enhancements make violations more detectable and support community confidence and regulatory oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permit term: public-facing transparency (real-time data websites)
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish public-facing websites with relevant compliance information and real-time data measurements about the facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public-facing data increases transparency and supports community awareness and empowerment; consider linking such portals to permit reporting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permit term: additional pollution controls or more stringent limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Require additional pollution controls or impose more stringent emission/discharge limits in permits where appropriate to reduce adverse impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stronger controls may be necessary where communities already bear disproportionate burdens or where health risks warrant stricter limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permit term: enforceable work practices, operating plans, and best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Include enforceable work practices, operating plans, or best practices (e.g., fugitive emissions plans) to minimize emissions and discharges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Making such practices enforceable ensures operational behaviors that reduce community exposures and environmental harms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permit term: make modeling assumptions enforceable (including operational conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate modeling assumptions as legally and practically enforceable limits or work practices (for example, specific hours of operation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reduces gap between modeled benefits and actual operations, and helps ensure modeled mitigations are implemented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permit term: expand buffers or modify operational hours
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider expanding buffer zones or modifying hours of operation as permit conditions to reduce community exposure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational adjustments can reduce community exposure patterns (e.g., avoid peak times when vulnerable populations are present).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use non-environmental authorities to implement mitigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage other authorities (public health, transportation, etc.) to implement mitigation measures that address adverse impacts in the community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include mobile health monitoring programs, new traffic plans to reduce diesel emissions, or citizen hotlines established through public health or transportation authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other commitments: third-party and community-driven monitoring and enforceable community agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursue third-party monitoring of community complaints, support transparency and community-driven monitoring, and consider enforceable agreements such as community benefit agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party monitoring and enforceable agreements can build trust, provide independent oversight, and create legally binding commitments to community protections or benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community engagement should be early, proactive, and meaningful
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct community engagement as soon as possible, going far beyond simply posting public notices; engagement should be active, proactive outreach that ensures those most affected have input into decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early engagement improves permit outcomes, builds relationships and trust, informs EJ screening and analyses, and supports meaningful consideration of site-specific circumstances. 'Meaningful involvement' includes informing, consulting, and working with affected communities throughout decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public involvement processes must be nondiscriminatory and accessible
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure public involvement processes are available to all persons regardless of race, color, national origin (including LEP status), disability, sex, age, or prior exercise of rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design outreach and participation mechanisms consistent with federal civil rights laws and EPA guidance to avoid excluding people on protected grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop and publish a public involvement plan (best practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Have written and published public involvement procedures consistent with federal civil rights laws and EPA’s Public Participation Guidance; tailor scope to staff size and resources but document procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public involvement plans should be prominent online and available in community locations; they should explain how residents can participate under various environmental laws and demonstrate the recipient's plan to provide meaningful access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe the affected community (demographics and background)
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a description of the relevant/affected community including demographics, history, and background (e.g., percent people of color, education levels, LEP populations, complaint history, internet access).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This description informs outreach strategy, LEP accommodations, accessibility planning, and identification of vulnerable populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide accessible contact information for public engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a contact list for relevant staff members on the recipient’s website, including phone numbers and email addresses, so the public can communicate via phone or internet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear contact points facilitate community input and responsiveness and should be maintained and publicized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document past and present community civil rights concerns and responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a list of past and present community civil rights concerns (including complaints filed under federal non-discrimination laws) and record actions taken in response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This historical record helps identify patterns of concern and guide appropriate responses and remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop and implement a detailed outreach plan and contingency plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a detailed plan of action (including outreach activities) to address public concerns and a contingency plan for unexpected events that impact public meetings or participation avenues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans should specify outreach timelines, responsible staff, alternative engagement methods (e.g., remote options), and processes for rapid adaptation during emergencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select meeting locations and times to enable meaningful involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify public meeting locations considering availability and schedules of public transportation and ensure meetings are held at times and in locations that allow meaningful involvement by LEP individuals and people with disabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider evenings/weekends, proximity to affected neighborhoods, transit access, childcare needs, and other barriers when scheduling meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide reasonable modifications, auxiliary aids, and language assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop and maintain plans to provide reasonable modifications and auxiliary aids at no cost for individuals with disabilities and language assistance services for LEP persons, including document translations and interpreters for meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document procedures for requesting accommodations, provide advance notice of available services, and budget/plan to deliver them reliably for all significant engagement activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use culturally and linguistically appropriate media outreach
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop and maintain a list of local media contacts tailored to the cultural and linguistic needs of the community to support outreach and notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targeted media outreach improves reach to LEP populations and communities that rely on non-traditional information channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure access for community members without internet
rubrics_metrics.description: Make public involvement plans and materials available in places easily accessible to the community (libraries, community centers) and ensure alternatives for those without internet access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide paper notices, phone hotlines, in-person distribution, and other non-digital channels to avoid excluding low-income or digitally disconnected residents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop public involvement plans with public input and prominent availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Public involvement plans should be developed with public input, highlighted online, and explain how residents can participate in the permitting process under various environmental laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Soliciting public input on the plan increases legitimacy and effectiveness; make the plan available in community-accessible locations and online.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public engagement elements to include in plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Plans should explain how the recipient will: (a) meaningfully engage the public before and during significant activities (including criteria for public hearings), (b) effectively communicate about programs and comment procedures, and (c) ensure public access to information and documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly document procedures for requesting hearings, public notice methods, how comments will be considered, and methods for distributing documents in accessible formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tribal consultation as government-to-government process
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct tribal consultation as a government-to-government process distinct from general community engagement, to obtain meaningful and timely input by tribal officials on actions that may affect tribes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tribal consultation fulfills federal trust responsibilities and is separate from public participation; states should coordinate with affected tribal governments and respect tribal consultation protocols.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA staff and manager responsibilities in permit review
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA staff and managers with permit issuance and review responsibilities should screen and review permits for potential EJ and civil rights issues, provide comments, and work with legal offices as needed to address potential adverse and disproportionate impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA is encouraged to provide technical assistance on civil rights compliance and to use its authority when reviewing permits issued by recipients of federal assistance. Staff should be alert to meaningful involvement and fair treatment concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients’ affirmative obligation to implement effective Title VI compliance programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients of EPA financial assistance acknowledge an affirmative obligation to implement effective Title VI compliance programs to ensure their actions do not involve discriminatory treatment or discriminatory effects even when facially neutral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should establish compliance procedures, monitor outcomes, maintain documentation, and address complaints and potential disparate impacts proactively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid discriminatory treatment in public processes (hearing equity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure public hearings and participation opportunities are scheduled, staffed, timed, and secured equitably across communities to avoid disparate treatment (e.g., equal number/length of hearings, equitable scheduling and staffing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of discriminatory treatment include offering more hearings, longer hearings, or better staffing in one part of town than another; equitable planning prevents inferences of intentional discrimination and promotes fair access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaningful involvement defined: inform, consult, and work with communities
rubrics_metrics.description: Meaningful involvement consists of informing, consulting, and working with potentially affected communities at various stages of environmental decision-making to address their questions and concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meaningful involvement is iterative and should occur throughout the permitting process, not only at a single point; it helps ensure decisions reflect site-specific community circumstances and supports Title VI compliance.
